name: Fieldstone wall corner
description: An L-shaped corner of village fieldstone wall, 0.45 m thick and 2.4 m high: rough grey-brown stone blocks in staggered courses over recessed mortar, tied by alternating quoins at a square corner pier, with flat capstones on top. One arm runs 0.75 m from the corner to +x, the other to +y, where they meet 1.5 m straight wall sections. The `_low` variant is a cutaway wall (about 1.4 m) for roofless village buildings, so what is inside stays visible. The `_rubble` variants (`_rubble`, `_rubble_2`, each also `_low`) are the same corner in rubble: rounded stones of mixed sizes, a long corner stone per course tying the arms, dark recessed joints, rounded cap stones; `_moss` adds moss on the caps and at the foot.

provenance.prompt: An L-shaped corner of the same village fieldstone wall as wall_stone_straight (about 0.45 m thick, 2.4 m high, rough grey-brown stone blocks in staggered courses, flat capstones on top). Footprint 1x1 tile: one arm runs from the tile centre to the +x edge, the other from the tile centre to the +y edge, joined in a square corner pier at the centre, so it meets straight sections (which run along x through the tile centre) at tile edges. Structure, static; blocks movement and sight, cover three-quarters, not destructible. Keep the triangle count well under budget.
